items.title: 68436_Alberta Hunter oral history interview
items.q: but she was married to Mr. Edgerton

ctx.x: my mother. I ran up the street, like I was going to ask my mother, and I came back and told her my mother said it was all right, I could go. So she said she was going to get on the train. She told me where to meet her down the street, so I met her down on the street, and we went down to the station. And I had on some blue shoes, some red shoes and a blue dress. And so she took me on into the station, and the man hollared, "All out for the northbound trains."

So Miss Florida -- her name was Florida Cummings -- her middle name -- maiden name was Florida Cummings, but she was married to Mr. Edgerton. So they took me on the train, and when they got on the train the conductor came around to get the tickets, and I was sitting between them. And he said to Miss Florida, "How old is this child?" She said, "She's eight years old." So he passed by; didn't say anything else and kept going.

So I knew a girl in Chicago by the name of Ellen Winston. Her mother and my mother knew each other. So when we got to Chicago, why I got off the streetcar -- we got on the streetcar, and I got off the streetcar on State Street. I know -- in front of a big building called the Burlington Building. Well, I didn't know where I was going, but I knew it was Chicago. So I got off the streetcar and left my schoolteacher and her husband on the car. Only God knows where I was going, but he led me right in front of this…
